About the Model

How CadenceGuard Predicts Pump Health

CadenceGuard uses a three-stage machine learning pipeline that processes hourly sensor telemetry from each pump — vibration, pressure, flow rate, temperature, and water-quality signals — to deliver real-time health scoring, maintenance timing, and failure-mode identification.

Stage 1

Anomaly Detection

Bottlenecked Autoencoder (MLP)

A sliding 24-hour window of sensor readings is fed into an autoencoder trained exclusively on healthy pump data. When the pump starts behaving abnormally, the autoencoder's reconstruction error rises — this error becomes a health score (0–1) that drives all downstream alerts.

Outputs → Health Score Normal Watch Warning Critical
Stage 2

Remaining Useful Life Estimation

Random Forest Regressor

Engineered features (rolling statistics, rate-of-change, cumulative stress) are combined with Stage 1's health score and fed into a regressor that predicts how many days remain before the pump will require maintenance. This drives the countdown ring shown for each pump.

Outputs → Days Until Maintenance
Stage 3

Failure Mode Classification

Random Forest Classifier

Using the same feature representation as Stage 2, a classifier determines the type of degradation occurring — mechanical wear (seal, impeller, bearing faults) or chemical corrosion (water-quality driven). Each failure type surfaces a tailored inspection checklist.

Outputs → Mechanical Chemical Normal
